biography.plain_text: Mikhail Prokhorov is a Russian investor who built his fortune through Norilsk Nickel during Russia's post-Soviet privatisation. A Moscow Finance Institute graduate, he founded ONEXIM Group after separating from business partner Vladimir Potanin. His investments also included the Brooklyn Nets basketball team, which he owned before selling to Joe Tsai.

long_biography.plain_text:
At Norilsk Nickel, Mikhail Prokhorov took responsibility for reshaping a sprawling metals producer. He shed non-core operations and helped separate its gold assets into Polyus Gold, creating a distinct business from interests previously held within the nickel group. His sale of the Norilsk stake before the global financial crisis left him with substantial funds for new investments.

With his sister Irina, a publisher, he established the Mikhail Prokhorov Foundation in 2004. It began in Norilsk, supporting theatre and contemporary art before extending its work across Siberia. The Krasnoyarsk Book Culture Fair combined book sales with public discussion, while his grant helped regional libraries buy books.

uncertainties: Current assessment date is 1 October 2026. The profile distinguishes original mining wealth from later investment interests; no legacy metal, sports or energy stake is automatically carried forward.

Finance & Investments is a medium-confidence inference from present wealth attribution, sustained investment activity and retained banking/insurance ownership. A complete personal asset breakdown and allocation of liquid proceeds are not public. This does not make bank gross assets or clients' money the owner's fortune.

The 2024 sale concerns the Russian Renaissance Capital entities and is distinct from the consumer bank Renaissance Credit. Mediana's 2026 transfer to Irina is excluded. These disposals qualify the broader current Forbes profile instead of being ignored.

Investor is independently supported by the continuing personal investment platform and deployment record. Founder and Passive asset owner were tested; historical delegation during politics alone does not establish current passivity, and the platform's age alone does not settle principal relationship.

Broad Self-made describes acquired and developed personal economics. Loans-for-shares and business-partner access are retained as material context. Neither an inherited family core nor an independent blank-slate start is inferred. The more precise initial capital and privileged-access subtype remains unresolved.

Current net worth, asset percentages and rankings are omitted from biographies. Divested Norilsk and Polyus holdings are explicitly historical; personal holdings are distinguished from company-wide values.

All supported personal profile types were checked: Instagram, LinkedIn, Personal Website, Facebook, Twitter, Youtube, TikTok, Vimeo, Flickr and Wikipedia, with Forbes first. Namesake LinkedIn accounts, generic Instagram biography claims, team clips and fan content were rejected. Twitter has two independent exact attributions despite restricted current access; no current posting claim is made.

The old personal domain and Facebook account remain candidates, not import proposals. ONEXIM domains were inaccessible and are not proposed as verified current company URLs. Foundation pages support research but are not substituted for a personal website. Trip Advisor and Zillow lack relevant fit.

The existing Wikipedia URL is unchanged. Birth date and patronymic come from the primary corporate biography; Moscow birthplace has lower confidence because the directly read corporate section supplies no city. Russian nationality and residence baseline are not rewritten from citizenship acquisition.

Five active tags form the minimum useful set for evidenced separate dimensions: Nickel mining, Gold mining, Investment banking, Insurance and Basketball. Generic Private equity would add overlap to the investment-platform description. Casual martial arts, recreational skiing, sponsorship and generic philanthropy do not yield tags.

Biographies omit unrequested political advocacy and irrelevant personal allegations. Privatisation remains in the short because it explains the wealth mechanism. Long-only industrial restructuring and regional cultural work are directly sourced, without attributing foundation staff's work solely to him.
